module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture relating two characterizations of a set of integers.

Informal Statement:
For an integer $k \ge 2$, the following are equivalent:

1. The greatest common divisor of the binomial coefficients
    $\binom{2k}{k}, \binom{3k}{k}, \dots, \binom{(k+1)k}{k} = 1$.

2. Writing prime factorization of $k$ as
    $k = \prod p_i^{e_i}$, and let
    $P = \max_i p_i^{e_i}$,
    one has $k / P > P$.

This conjecture asserts that the sequence defined by 1. is obtained by
taking 1 off each number in the sequence defined by 2.

*References:*
- [A80170](https://oeis.org/A80170)
- [A51283](https://oeis.org/A51283)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA80170

/--
The gcd of the binomial coefficients
$\binom{2k}{k}, \binom{3k}{k}, \dots, \binom{(k+1)k}{k} = 1$.
-/
def A (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (Finset.range k).gcd (fun i => Nat.choose ((i + 2) * k) k) = 1

/--
Let $P$ be the largest prime power dividing `k`.
Then $k / P > P$.
-/
def B (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  let P := ((Nat.divisors k).filter IsPrimePow).max.getD 0
  k / P > P

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : ¬A 2 := by unfold A; decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : ¬A 3 := by unfold A; decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : ¬A 4 := by unfold A; decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : ¬A 5 := by unfold A; decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_6 : ¬A 6 := by unfold A; decide

/--
Conjecture: The gcd condition is equivalent to the prime power condition.
This has been conjectured by Ralf Stephan.

Both the natural-language proof and its Lean 4 formalization were carried out
by the KLMM MechMath Agent Team; see the `formal_proof` attribute.

*References:*
- [Ralf Stephan, *Prove or Disprove. 100 Conjectures from the OEIS*, 2004, Conjecture 17 (arXiv:math/0409509)](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0409509)
- [Dakai Guo et al., *A Greatest Common Divisor Criterion of Certain Binomial Coefficients*, 2026 (arXiv:2606.22997)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22997)
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/guodk/formal-conjectures/blob/0720658844d76a50d48e4baa152eef14d4462907/FormalConjectures/OEIS/80170.lean#L1823"]
theorem gcdCondition_iff_primePowerCondition (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    A k ↔ B (k + 1) := by
  sorry

end OeisA80170

findings.description: The module docstring (lines 24–32) says the two conditions at the same k are equivalent, i.e. A k ↔ B k. The source and the Lean theorem instead assert A k ↔ B (k + 1). This is a substantive error in the prose only: Lean evaluation gives A 29 = true, B 29 = false, and B 30 = true. The docstring's subsequent sentence about subtracting one correctly describes the shift.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A080170 states “a(n) = A051283(n) - 1,” and A051283 defines its condition using the factorization of its own argument. Records read via https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A080/A080170.seq and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A051/A051283.seq. Guo et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22997, Theorem 1, explicitly puts n = k + 1 and states D(k) = 1 iff n/ppart(n) > ppart(n).
findings.suggested_fix: Keep both predicate definitions and the theorem unchanged. Replace “the following are equivalent” in the module docstring with “consider the following two conditions,” then explicitly state that condition 1 at k is equivalent to condition 2 at k + 1.

reformulations.difference: Lean maximizes over all prime-power divisors and uses natural-number division, whereas the source maximizes the complete components p_i^e_i of the prime factorization and writes ordinary division.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n ≥ 2, the filtered divisor set is nonempty. Every prime-power divisor p^j has j ≤ v_p(n), and every complete component p^v_p(n) belongs to that set, so the two maxima coincide. The maximum P is positive and divides n; consequently natural-number division n / P is exact and agrees with rational division. The main theorem applies B only to n = k + 1 ≥ 3, excluding the empty/default cases. Both the maximum identity and the resulting equivalence with the rational-division formulation were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean using only standard axioms.

review.notes: No misformalized Lean declaration was found: both definitions, all five tests, and the main theorem are faithful. Boundary values and the first sequence terms were checked, and A k agreed with B (k + 1) for every 2 ≤ k ≤ 300. The gcd reindexing was also proved in Lean. Direct OEIS pages were blocked by Cloudflare, so the complete records were read from the official OEIS data mirror. A080170's June 29, 2026 comment records the proof, matching the solved tag. The pinned proof was compiled in a scratch copy with its old import path updated; a namespace-renamed copy directly proved the current statement. Its axioms were exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].
